questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- A beautiful city with significant history.
- A historical faculty at the host university.
- Not too expensive to live in.
- Decent dorm opportunities.
- The host university does not require learning a new language to study there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people were extremely helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an information meeting, and it was possible to schedule office hours with coordinators.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was organized through the university's dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The area where the dorm is can be quite barren, so make sure to travel into the city regularly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For the price it was really good, and i made friends for life so no complaints.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We went to the faculty for registration, and formed a line. It was smooth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Two erasmus coordinators were there to answer any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was about being as fast as possible as soon as registration opened. I only missed out on one class that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be patient and perhaps try to talk to your fellow students while waiting. It can be a good introduction to socialization..

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very solid. Would have perhaps liked less emphasis on class presentations, and more on fluid discussion/debate.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were MA courses, but for some of them, BA students could also attend.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As I previously mentioned, less emphasis on debate/discussion and more time devoted to individual presentations. For me, this discouraged the class in engaging with every text each week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Symbolic Poem - Keats
Southern Literature
Writing as an Experiment
British Literature of the Asian and African Diaspora
Samuel Beckett: the Plays

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of the courses, but my personal favourites were Symbolic Poem - Keats and Samuel Beckett. The lecturers were great.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Using the washing machine in the dorm (not unexpected, but might be worth noting).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was cheaper than Denmark, which was nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a local sports centre near my dorm, and some sports classes are available.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a bunch of opportunities, but I didn't sign up for that much, I focused on efforts organized externally by students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Keep an eye on film festivals, semester opening events, perhaps try going to an ice hockey game or some other sport events. I really enjoyed playing volleyball and football with fellow students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try to also visit other towns outside Prague. I had some amazing memories in Karlovy Vary, Cesky Krumlov and Budapest. All stunning and doable for a weekend trip, or even daytrip. Other students have raved about Vienna, Warsaw, Dresden, Brno, Plzen. There are so many options in the vicinity. Take advantage of Prague's proximity to these fantastic places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy for me personally. But it all depends on personality types I believe, and it's very important to make an effort to get along with your roommate, even if just on a superficial, friendly level.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out of your room. Sometimes just showing up to an event or in a common area will mean you make a friend for life.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In my opinion Czechs seem similar to Danes in that they are introverted to a degree, until alcohol is involved. Therefore it wasn't such a culture shock. But if you don't drink, then try to discover what events are going on that don't involve drinking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are always down to do things. Sometimes all it takes is asking, reaching out. People are on erasmus to make friends, just like you, so don't be too shy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Try to make a list of goals/things you would like to do before you leave, and keep those in mind while you are on exchange. Time flies fast, don't let it pass you by.
- Be kind and accommodating during your stay. You are a guest in another country, you should expect having to acclimatize to the country a bit, not the other way around. If things aren't the exact way you expected, don't let it defeat you.
- Enjoy it. It's one of the most exciting times you'll ever have. Don't overthink it too much, live in the moment and be present.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Jana Palacha 2 is a beautiful building. That's all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably juggling academic workload/social desires. It's hard to be satisfied with both simultaneously.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
